title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j
talk_summary: A Neo4j workshop showing three 'shapes' for grounding an agent: a metadata/semantic-layer graph over a SQL warehouse (join paths), a deterministic document containment tree with hierarchical URIs plus full-text search, and Leiden community detection to surface themes. The core claim is that graph structure (not just vector search) lets agents answer estate-level and 'prove a negative' questions and traverse documents instead of doing many probabilistic vector hits.

takeaways.technique: Metadata/semantic-layer graph for SQL join paths
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a graph of just the warehouse metadata (database→schema→tables→columns, plus reference join paths) and expose it via MCP so the agent reads join paths before writing text-to-SQL, instead of ETLing data into the graph.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're not using the graph to copy the data over... we're using the graph as a semantic layer. So we're just pulling metadata about the columns

takeaways.technique: Deterministic document tree with hierarchical URIs + scoped full-text search
takeaways.what_they_do: Load docs as an idempotent containment tree (library→folder→doc→section) with next-section and cross-links, give every node a hierarchical URI, then run Lucene full-text search post-filtered by URI prefix to scope search to a subtree.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's all deterministic with the containment tree for one and then the ordering of the sections as well as the links

takeaways.technique: Spec-first query authoring (write the shape, then let agent write the query)
takeaways.what_they_do: For complex queries they write a human-readable spec of the desired output shape in a docs file, then instruct the agent to implement against that spec using a domain skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'll write a spec for it... I have my outline format spec where I say this is the shape

takeaways.technique: Vendor-maintained domain skills to avoid stale training data
takeaways.what_they_do: Install a CLI plus curated skill files (query language, graph data science) so the agent uses current syntax instead of hallucinating from years-old Stack Overflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to go on the internet and get the Stack Overflow questions from like four or five or six years ago and it's going to give you outdated bad cipher

takeaways.technique: Graph community detection to find coverage gaps / prove negatives
takeaways.what_they_do: Run Leiden on the document link graph to cluster docs into themes, then correlate themes against warehouse work-order data to find undocumented codes and mismatched procedures — questions similarity search can't answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't really search for a negative. You have to search for things that are there

takeaways.technique: Keep structured and unstructured graphs separate; agent joins at query time
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately did not link the SQL metadata graph and the document graph; the agent extracts a key (part/code) from one and looks it up in the other, doing the join in real time.
